thread:
Maya Chen: quick share — ran a compact regional bench (eu-west / us-west / ap-southeast) comparing L4 / T4 / A10G for embeddings and small-chat. short summary below, asking for kernel/packing recs and obvious gotchas.
Liam O'Connor: nice, drop the raw numbers pls.
Maya Chen: pasted the runner output below (script: bench/region_mosaic_v2.sh). kept quant at q4_0 for embeddings and q4_1 for small-chat, CPU fallback off.
bench-bot: automated results attached:
```
--- EMBEDDINGS (mean across 1k requests, 512-dim)
region | GPU  | p50_lat(ms) | p95_lat(ms) | qps_per_gpu | cost_per_1M_tokens_est
EU-W  | L4   | 8.2         | 15.6        | 1200        | $9.4
EU-W  | T4   | 12.1        | 28.3        | 760         | $6.2
EU-W  | A10G | 7.6         | 13.2        | 1360        | $11.1
--- SMALL-CHAT (avg 64-token responses, 512 context)
region | GPU  | p50_lat(ms) | p95_lat(ms) | tokens/s_gpu | cost_per_1M_tokens_est
US-W  | L4   | 48          | 120         | 1400         | $10.8
US-W  | T4   | 66          | 210         | 850          | $6.7
US-W  | A10G | 38          | 95          | 1900         | $14.9
```
Maya Chen: raw logs show A10G gives best latency across small-chat but is most expensive, L4 is a solid middle ground with better throughput for embeddings. T4 is cheapest but P95 is much noisier.
Anika Roy: what kernels did you run? flash-attn / cutlass / triton variants?
Maya Chen: default runtime chose cutlass-int8 kernels for L4/A10G for embeddings, flash-attn for attention in small-chat on A10G, and a fallback path (vectorized) on T4. I forced flash-attn on T4 and saw ~10% p50 drop but p95 still spiky.
Liam O'Connor: what about KV cache sizing/packing? were we batching or continuous single-req?
Maya Chen: mixed. embeddings: large batching (up to 512) to saturate throughput. small-chat: continuous single-req latency with dynamic batching up to 8. KV cache hit ratio ~85% in small-chat tests.
Dave Patel: capacity notes — for eu-west embeddings at 1M qps/day target, L4 pools need ~12 GPUs (binpack factor 0.85) vs A10G ~10 GPUs. T4 would need ~18 GPUs. cost numbers assume reserved prices + avg util 70%.
Anika Roy: any quality regressions when switching quant levels? q4_0 -> q4_1 for small-chat can change safety tokenization?
Maya Chen: we ran eval suite (200 prompt pairs) — q4_1 small-chat had 2.3% drop in semantic score vs fp16 baseline on some tricky coref cases. embeddings were stable (NDCG drop <0.4%).
Liam O'Connor: interesting. So trade is latency/cost vs small drop in chat quality. Can we do hybrid? A10G for chat, L4 for embeddings?
Maya Chen: that's my recommended routing policy: chat -> region:A10G primary, fallback:L4; embeddings -> L4 primary, T4 as cheap fallback for non-critical bulk jobs.
sre-bot: note: traffic routing rules will create hotspot on A10G in us-west if you don't shard by customer. add per-customer routing and circuit-breaker thresholds.
Dave Patel: kernel caveat — on L4 we saw memory fragmentation on long-run embedding jobs using the cutlass-int8 path. a weekly recycler job (docker restart) cleared it, but we should look at allocator flags.
Anika Roy: any tips for packing? small-chat with 64-token responses benefited from microbatching requests of similar length. suggest bucketed batching + length-aware packing in the runtime.
Maya Chen: agree. final takeaways: 1) A10G = best latency for small-chat, expensive; 2) L4 = best cost/throughput sweet spot for embeddings and mixed workloads; 3) T4 = cheapest per-hour but higher variance — good for best-effort bulk embedding backfills; 4) quant/metric: use q4_1 for embeddings, hold fp16/q4_0 for critical chat paths until we expand eval coverage.
Liam O'Connor: can you drop the bench script and the eval set link? I'll run it in ap-southeast later.
Maya Chen: added script + eval link in the thread: https://redwood-internal/bench/mosaic-v2 and https://redwood-internal/eval/mosaic-chat-200. will run ap-southeast on your ticket.
bench-bot: created ticket BENCH-4321 for ap-southeast run and noted kernel flags.
Maya Chen: thanks — any other objections before I add the routing policy to the canary config?
Anika Roy: go ahead, but add safety canary: 10% traffic, 2-minute rollback, and compare eval metrics automatically.
Maya Chen: will do. :thumbsup:
